title: helm(private): values schema & init hooks - stabilize upgrade/rollback behavior and templating fixes
author: Ethan Brooks
description:
Motivation: customers running Redwood Private in air-gapped/VPC environments reported upgrade failures when the init-values hook mutated values in ways that were incompatible with existing CRs and node affinity constraints. This PR stabilizes the Helm values schema, tightens validation, and refactors init/job hooks to be idempotent for rolling upgrades and rollbacks.

Summary of changes: consolidated values.schema.json with clearer required fields for encryption/KMS, tolerations, and nodeSelector; added migration notes for deprecated fields; updated templates to avoid mutable defaults during upgrades; introduced explicit pre-upgrade and post-rollback hook jobs that validate cluster constraints before patching; improved helm tests to cover upgrade->rollback scenarios.

Compatibility: this is a non-breaking upgrade for new installs. Existing installs that relied on implicit defaulting of .private.kmsKeyName or on mutable tolerations should follow the migration steps in release_notes before upgrading.

Checklist: [x] values schema update and validation [x] idempotent init hooks [x] upgrade/rollback e2e test coverage [x] changelog/release notes [x] docs update (values reference)
commits: refactor(helm): split values.schema.json into stable and v2 sections
feat(helm): add pre-upgrade init hook to validate nodeAffinity and KMS availability
fix(helm): avoid rewriting .private.tolerations on upgrade (preserve user-provided values)
test(helm): add e2e upgrade->rollback scenario in perf-canary pipeline
chore(docs): document migration steps for deprecated fields
files_diff_snippets: values.schema.json: tightened 'kms' object - required: ['enabled','provider'] and removed permissive pattern matching
init-values-job.yaml: job now exits successfully when all validations pass; uses --dry-run flag before applying patches
pre-upgrade-validate.yaml: new hook (helm.sh/hook: pre-upgrade) checks nodeSelector/tolerations and KMS connectivity
_helpers.tpl: add defaultIfUndefined helper to avoid overriding user-provided values
upgrade-rollback-test.yaml: new harness simulates canary node drain, upgrade, and rollback
review_thread: Ava Chen: Found a failure case when KMS is disabled but kmsKeyName is set; suggested stronger schema validation - addressed in commit 3
Diego Martinez: Requested to make hooks idempotent so `helm upgrade --force` doesn't reapply patches repeatedly - changed init-job to be noop when values already match
Priya Nair: Asked for explicit migration notes for customers with custom tolerations; added docs/private/values-reference.md section and release notes
Liam O'Connor: Ran e2e upgrade test and reported a transient failure on first run; CI fix pushed to retry helm hooks with backoff (commit 4)
testing_notes: Local helm-lint and chart rendering validated for k8s 1.25/1.26. Ran private-installer end-to-end in a VPC test account with both KMS and file-based encryption. Added perf-canary pipeline job that exercises upgrade -> rollback path; initial flaky runs addressed by adding hook retry/backoff logic.
migration_steps: 1) Read docs/private/values-reference.md. 2) If you set .private.kms.enabled=false but still have .private.kms.keyName populated, remove the keyName or enable KMS. 3) For custom tolerations/nodeSelector, add them under .private.nodeSelector and .private.tolerations explicitly to avoid Helm applying defaults. 4) Run helm upgrade with --wait and confirm pre-upgrade hook succeeds before proceeding.
rollback_plan: If the pre-upgrade hook fails or the upgrade behaves unexpectedly, run 'helm rollback <release> <revision>' which will trigger post-rollback-validate hook to verify cluster invariants. If hooks fail, follow the documented manual rollback steps in docs/private/values-reference.md to revert values and restart the installer pod.
release_notes:
- Stabilize Helm values schema for Redwood Private (charts/redwood-private).
- Add pre-upgrade and post-rollback validation hooks to reduce failed upgrades in VPC/on-prem installs.
- Make init-values job idempotent and non-destructive during upgrades.
- Document migration steps for KMS and tolerations/nodeSelector fields.
